To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
immunodominant peptide immunotherapy can reduce the human anti‐TT IgG antibody response in hu‐PRL‐SCID mice.

(1) the hu‐P‐SCID model can be used to test the efficacy of immunodominent peptides in reducing antibody responses in humans and (2) peptides corresponding to the major T cell epitope of tetanus toxid reduced the anti‐tetanus antibody response in hu‐P‐S‐mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of peptides corresponding to immunodominant T cell epitopes to modulate the immune response in vivo.
the development of immunotherapy for the reduction of human anti‐TT antibody by the administration of peptides that correspond to the immunodominant epitopes of TT.
the use of immunodominance as a strategy to reduce the production of antibodies against common allergens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of this study show that it is feasible to use a preclinical model to examine the effect of immunotherapy with peptides on the long‐terminal antibody response to TT in humans.
the hu‐ PBL‐SCID mouse model is an excellent tool for studying human T‐cell responses and for testing immunomodulation strategies in a preclinical setting.
this is a very interesting and potentially useful model system for the study of human antibody responses to tetanus toxoid in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
peptide immunotherapy may have potential in reducing the human immune response to TT.
the hu‐SCID mouse model system is a useful pre‐clinical model for testing the efficacy of peptide‐mediated immunotherapy for reduction or elimination of pathological antibody responses in humans.
this is a very interesting and important model, but the data presented in the article are not sufficient to support the conclusions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of immunodominance to reduce antibody responses is a viable approach to immunotherapy of allergic and autoimmune disease.
we have demonstrated that it is possible to reduce the human antibody response in a mouse model.

we have developed a model for testing the effect of immunotherapy in humans, using immunodominant epitopes of a common antigen, in this case tetanus toxoid, in a mouse model of human immune responses.
